assertions.text: createWorktree(workspace, runId, itemId) runs `git worktree add` at exactly <stateHome>/conductor/<workspaceKey>/worktrees/<runId>/<itemId> and returns that path, with each id segment guarded by assertSafeId (a traversing runId or itemId is REFUSED before any git call, because the path is later removed and pruned); the branch is created EXPLICITLY as conductor/<runId>/<itemId> — a bare `git worktree add` would name it after the path basename and collide across runs — and the main repo's HEAD, status and branch are unchanged by the call

removeWorktree(workspace, runId, itemId) removes the worktree AND its branch: `git worktree list` no longer names the path, the directory is gone, and `git branch --list` no longer carries conductor/<runId>/<itemId> (asserted separately, because `git worktree remove --force` leaves the branch behind); when the directory was already deleted the prune fallback still clears the administrative entry; afterwards the main repo's status is clean and HEAD is untouched

the created worktree path is OUTSIDE the repo root (not a prefix-descendant of workspace), and the main tree's whole-tree verify provably does NOT execute the worktree's copy of a test: a deliberately-red, witness-file-writing test present in the worktree leaves a main-tree runVerify green with the witness file absent — the Task 6.2 hazard (a worktree inside the repo is a second copy of every test file) closed by construction

DEFERRED BINDING (C-021, phaseGate4Bindings), one behaviour pinned: registerConductorExclude resolves the exclude file through `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (resolved against root when git returns the relative ".git") and writes the single `.conductor/` line there. Called with a LINKED worktree root it does NOT throw ENOTDIR (root/.git is a FILE there, and the isRepo guard does not catch it because rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree returns true), creates NO .git/info directory inside the worktree, and the exclusion is EFFECTIVE — `git status --porcelain` inside the worktree does not list .conductor/. The per-worktree gitdir is NOT used as the target: an exclude written there is inert. Main-repo behaviour is unchanged and still idempotent

under parallel.writes "worktrees", conductor_dispatch_wave creates one worktree per wave implementer and persists item.worktree (the committed §2.5 field) = that path, read back via store.loadItem and journaled as `state: item.updated`; under the default "off" no worktree is created, no worktree git command runs at all, and item.worktree stays null

the session registry entry for a wave implementer carries tree = its worktree PATH, and the edit gate then scopes edits to that tree: an edit to <worktree>/src/covered.ts with fileScope src/** is ALLOWED (tree-relative normalization, never false-denied because the worktree lives under the state home), while the same relative path in the MAIN tree and in a sibling item's worktree is DENIED for that session

evidence.runVerify for a worktree item runs with cwd = the worktree and tree = the item id: the §2.6 verify record carries tree "<itemId>" plus the WORKTREE's head and branch (not the workspace's), and the per-tree marker file is verify-running-<itemId>.json in the run dir — Task 6.1 machinery reused, not reimplemented

C-037 ruling 5, the slug/path bridge: the evidence layer's tree is an ITEM-ID SLUG (markerPathOf runs assertSafeId, which rejects "/") while the gate's tree is a PATH compared by string equality, so the gate-wiring layer MUST translate before it fills verifyInFlightTree. Asserted end-to-end: with a live marker verify-running-I1.json and a session registered with tree = I1's worktree PATH, decideEdit DENIES every edit in that session (frozen); feeding the raw slug through instead leaves the session UNFROZEN, which is the defect this row exists to prevent. The translation reads the item's `worktree` field (null -> no path is frozen for that item), and assertSafeId is NOT relaxed — markerPathOf still refuses a path-shaped tree

a LIVE verify marker in tree A does not freeze tree B: while A's marker is live, decideEdit denies every edit in A (source, test and config alike, the §3.5:1396-1401 strict reading) but ALLOWS a B-scoped edit in B, and the fan-out TreeState admission does not hold B's write-capable dispatch

conductor_publish under worktree mode runs the §3.3 sequence — branch check against the WORKTREE's verify record head, stage fileScope ∪ testScope minus run.startDirty, format, freshness, commit — with cwd = item.worktree: the commit lands on the worktree's branch conductor/<runId>/<itemId>, and the workspace's HEAD, index and branch are unchanged until merge-back runs

worktree mode changes the cwd, never the commit discipline: the message is the same pure core/ template output (zero model dispatches recorded by the fake SDK) and the §3.3 trailer denylist — Co-Authored-By, Signed-off-by, 'Generated with', U+1F916, case-insensitive — is enforced on the worktree commit exactly as in the main tree

mergeBack(workspace, runId, itemId) merges the branch built by the SAME pure name builder createWorktree used (conductor/<runId>/<itemId>), and it VERIFIES that name against gitio.currentBranch(item.worktree) before running any merge — a worktree whose checked-out branch does not match is REFUSED with no merge attempted, so a renamed or stale branch can never be merged silently. The two-argument sketch at plan 2706 cannot compose the name; the runId comes from the handler's run context

ff-only is attempted FIRST and a normal merge is only the fallback (§4.2:1613): a fixture whose workspace branch has not advanced since the worktree was created integrates as a fast-forward and produces NO merge commit; a fixture whose workspace branch HAS advanced with a disjoint-scope commit falls back to a normal merge and produces exactly one merge commit — asserted on the resulting history shape, not on a log line

merge-back is serial in ITEM ORDER (§4.2:1613, §4.3:1627 — the workspace index is a singleton): with a two-item disjoint-scope fixture, both items' commits end up reachable from the workspace branch, merged in item order, and the second merge never begins before the first has completed (asserted on the ordered command log; no two merges are ever in flight in the workspace)

every merge-back git operation is executed by the HANDLER through execFileSync argv arrays under gitio's GIT_ENV scrub — never a shell string, never a model session (core/gates-git.ts denies a session's merge/commit/push) — and a clean integration returns exactly {ok:true, conflict:false} for each item

after each merge-back the item re-validates against the INTEGRATED tree before PUBLISHED: a runVerify with cwd = workspace and tree "main" provably executes there (witness file written by the fixture verify command in the workspace, absent from every worktree), and the item does not reach PUBLISHED without that integrated-tree verify succeeding — a green in isolation is not a green in company

a contrived overlapping edit makes the LATER item's merge conflict: mergeBack returns {ok:false, conflict:true} and the later item is demoted to GREEN through the SHARED 9.5b demotion helper — the persisted item read back via store.loadItem shows GREEN with the debugging annotation set, the journal carries `state: item.updated` and ZERO fsm records for that write (the FSM has no backward edge), and the EARLIER item's completed merge still stands in the workspace

the conflicting merge leaves the workspace USABLE: mergeBack runs `git merge --abort` before returning, so afterwards there is no MERGE_HEAD, `git status --porcelain` is clean, no conflict markers remain in any tracked file, and a subsequent merge-back of an unrelated item succeeds in that same workspace — a poisoned mid-merge tree would break every later merge and every integrated-tree verify

C-037 ruling 6, asserted as a regression pin: adapter/state.ts archiveRun(runId) clears the current-run pointer and removes NOTHING — after archiving, the run's worktrees still appear in `git worktree list` and <stateHome>/conductor/<workspaceKey>/worktrees/<runId>/ still exists on disk. Worktree removal is adapter/worktrees.ts's removeWorktree, invoked by the run-lifecycle owner (Task 10.1); state.ts gains no adapter-to-adapter edge and no deletion behaviour

a crashed run that left a worktree DIRECTORY deleted but its administrative entry behind (fixture: rm -rf the worktree dir, keep the .git/worktrees metadata) never wedges a later run: the next createWorktree runs `git worktree prune` BEFORE adding and then succeeds in adding the new worktree — crash healing at the next worktree operation, no daemon and no new persisted state

§3.9:1503 (no-git disables worktree mode): in a workspace where gitio.isRepo is false, createWorktree REFUSES naming no-git mode — no directory is created under <stateHome>/conductor/<workspaceKey>/worktrees/, no git command is attempted, and item.worktree stays null — so a no-git run can never be handed a worktree path the rest of the pipeline would then treat as a tree
